title: Spotting Counterfeit Whisky | Craft Beer School
desc: How to spot counterfeit whisky in India: seals, excise labels, bottle details, a simple strength check at home and what to do if you suspect a fake.
teaser: A broken seal, a smudged label or a reading of 30% on a 42.8% bottle. Here is how to check.
standfirst: Fake and tampered whisky reaches shelves and bars in India and abroad. Most of it can be caught with a careful look and a few simple checks. Here is what to examine before you open a bottle and what to do if something feels wrong.
sections:
Counterfeit whisky comes in two broad forms. A refill is a genuine bottle, emptied and refilled with something cheaper, then resealed. A forgery is a fake from the start: copied bottle, copied label, unknown contents. Refills can turn up at any price. Forgeries are usually aimed at bottles valuable enough to be worth copying.

Both can be caught. The checks below start at the shop counter and finish in your kitchen.
Check the seal and the excise label

Most Indian states require an excise adhesive label or hologram on every bottle. Many now carry a code you can scan or check online. Make sure it is present, intact and not peeled and restuck. A label stuck over a torn older one is a warning sign.

Look at the cap. Many bottles use a pilfer-proof cap with a ring that breaks on first opening. If the ring is already loose or the cap turns too easily, do not buy it. Some bottles also have a non-refillable fitment in the neck. If yours should have one and does not, ask questions.
Read the bottle as closely as the label

Compare the bottle with one you know is genuine, or with clear photos from the producer. Check the printing: blurred text, spelling mistakes, crooked labels and colours that look washed out are common in forgeries. Look for batch codes lasered onto the glass or printed on the label and check that they match.

Fill level should be consistent across bottles of the same brand. Look for sediment, cloudiness or an unusual colour. Glass embossing, the weight of the bottle and the quality of the box all tell you something. Our guide to whisky label terms helps you read the rest.
Use your nose and a hydrometer

Pour a small measure into a nosing glass and smell it before you drink. A genuine whisky should smell like the style it claims to be. A sharp solvent smell, a thin, watery nose or a flavour that does not match previous bottles are warning signs.

A spirit hydrometer, sometimes sold as an alcoholmeter, is cheap and reads the strength of a spirit at its calibration temperature, usually 20 °C. Many Indian whiskies are bottled at 42.8% ABV, the old 75 degrees proof. If yours reads 30%, it has almost certainly been watered. Whisky's small amount of dissolved solids can make the reading slightly low, but not by that much.
Illicit liquor is a poisoning risk

The most dangerous fakes are not watered whisky but illicit spirit, which can contain methanol. Methanol poisoning can cause blindness and death. Symptoms can be delayed by hours.

If anyone feels very unwell, has blurred vision or severe stomach pain after drinking suspect liquor, get medical help at once. Do not wait to see if it passes. Buying only from licensed shops and bars is the simplest protection.

Buy from licensed shops and keep the bill. Be wary of unusually low prices, bottles from unofficial sellers and offers on social media. A rare bottle at half its usual price is almost never a bargain.

In bars, a whisky that tastes very different from the same brand elsewhere can be a sign of a refilled bottle. Telling that confidently depends on knowing what the real thing tastes like, which is a trained skill rather than a hunch.
What to do if you suspect a fake

Stop drinking it. Keep the bottle, the cap and the bill. Report it to your state excise department or the consumer helpline. Tell the shop or bar too. Many brands also have a consumer line for reporting suspected counterfeits.

Do not pour it away until you have reported it. The bottle is the evidence.

If you bought it in a bar, ask to see the bottle and note the brand, the batch code and the date. A polite question at the counter is often enough to get a refund or a different pour. It also tells the bar that customers are paying attention.
Check your next bottle before you open it

Next time you buy a whisky, spend two minutes before you open it. Check the excise label, the cap ring, the printing and the fill level. Smell the first pour carefully.

If you drink whisky regularly, buy a spirit hydrometer and test one bottle. Knowing what a genuine reading looks like makes a fake much easier to spot.
faqs: How can I tell if whisky is fake in India?
Check the excise label or hologram, the cap seal, the print quality and the fill level. Buy from licensed shops and keep the bill.
Can I test whisky strength at home?
Yes. A spirit hydrometer reads the strength at its calibration temperature. A reading far below the label suggests the whisky has been watered.
What should I do if I suspect fake whisky?
Stop drinking it, keep the bottle and bill and report it to the state excise department or consumer helpline. Seek medical help at once if anyone feels unwell.
